Agent 3 downloaded ~40 WER cholera annual reviews this way and text-extracted them with pdftotext -layout. This is the highest-value tooling discovery of the MRT run.

Agent 3: WHO changed its annual cholera reporting format at 2016-2017. From then on, countries that ACTIVELY notify zero are named in a separate 'zero reporting' list. Before 2016 no such category existed (verified: zero matches for 'zero reporting' in every annual review 2008-2014). Consequence: pre-2016, absence from Table 1 means a notified zero; post-2016, absence from BOTH the case table and the zero list means the country filed nothing. Mauritania zero-reported in 2018, 2022, 2023, 2024 and filed nothing in 2016, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021.

Agent 3 TRAP: WER 'Cholera, 2005' states 'Mauritania and the Gambia, which had both been free of cholera for a decade, were also affected by outbreaks'. A decade-long zero row built on that sentence would erase a 4534-case epidemic.

MODEL-PATH FINDING (orchestrator, from reading py/build_weekly_timeseries.py and MOSAIC-pkg/R/process_AI_cholera_data.R): MOSAIC-pkg consumes ONLY data/MRT/cholera_weekly_MRT.csv. The builder uses national rows only (Location exactly AFR::MRT), resolves each ISO week by source priority WHO > JHU > AI, and builds the seasonal template from JHU+WHO weekly rows only (MRT has no positive JHU weekly rows, so it borrows the West Africa regional template). Therefore an AI national row inside any JHU-covered year (positive: 1971-73, 1984-89, 1996-97, 2002-03, 2005-07, 2011; zero: 2012-2024) is overwritten week-by-week and does not change the model input; sub-national rows are never read. AI rows reach the model ONLY in AI-only periods: 1970, 1974-1983, 1990-1995, 1998-2001, 2004, 2008-2010, and 2025-01-01 onward (incl. the open 2026-09 gap). Priority for this run follows from that; sub-annual/sub-national work in JHU years is data-product value (and future-builder value), not current model input.
